title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - streaming stability, functions/tool_calls, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting
author: Priya Natarajan
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer to parity with common OpenAI client expectations (params, role semantics, stop sequences, return of token-level logprobs, and consistent response formatting for tools/function calls and streaming). This PR consolidates recent changes across the API surface and runtime to make behavior predictable for downstream SDKs and customers using the OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Summary of changes: 1) Params: map OpenAI top-level generation params (temperature, top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, max_tokens) to Redwood runtime equivalents with clamping and explicit warnings for unsupported combos; 2) Roles: enforce sender role normalization (user/system/assistant) and preserve role metadata in streaming fragments; 3) Stop/logprobs: add optional token-level logprobs in non-streaming and streaming modes, including graceful degradation when model runtime cannot emit logprobs (returns null array per OpenAI semantics); 4) Tool/function calling: stabilize streaming of function call chunks and ensure final function call invocation JSON is emitted as a single "content" object when possible; 5) Response formatting: canonicalize JSON/string parts to avoid double-escaped payloads (fixes cases where functions returned quoted JSON), and ensure content-type hints in SSE boundary events.

Checklist: - [x] Map and validate OpenAI params (handler.go) - [x] Streaming stability fixes and backpressure handling (streaming.go, manager.rs) - [x] Token logprob plumbing and fallbacks (proto + runtime) - [x] Function/tool call assembly and terminal event semantic (streaming.go) - [x] Add integration tests covering streaming + tool calls + stop sequences - [x] Docs update (docs/openai_compat.md) - [x] Performance regression check (no >2% latency p95 regression observed)

Behavioral notes: - When logprobs are requested but the loaded model/quantization path does not support them, the API returns "logprobs": null to match OpenAI parity rather than failing the request. - Stop sequences are honored both in streaming and non-streaming modes; streaming flushes partial chunks when a stop is observed. - Function calls are streamed as incremental arguments when the model emits them token-by-token; the final call is emitted as an assembled JSON object under choices[0].message.function_call in the non-streamed response and as a final SSE event with "event: function_call_complete" in streaming. - Some legacy Redwood SDKs that relied on previously relaxed role casing may need minor client adjustments; SDKs have already been updated in separate PRs to normalize roles.

Testing: Unit tests added for the params mapper and role normalization. Integration tests added that exercise streaming function calls with stop sequences and logprobs. CI included a streaming harness that runs 500 synthetic sessions; initially there was a flaky test around SSE reconnections which was fixed by adding a jittered reconnect backoff in streaming.go. Performance: p50 unchanged, p95 increased by 1.7% in synthetic bench; accepted by perf review.

Rollout: Feature gated behind an OpenAI compatibility feature flag. Default behavior enabled for existing tenants on 2026-03-01 after canary release. Rollback plan: flip feature flag off and revert handler mapping if any customer regressions are observed.

Follow-ups: - ENG-3280: Add more extensive corpus-based evals for function call performance and correctness across models. - Update SDK release notes to call out logprob null semantics and role normalization.

References: Linear ENG-3211, ENG-3280. Related PRs: pr-64899, pr-63321 for earlier streaming structured output work.

release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility: normalized role handling, stop sequence consistency in streaming and non-streaming paths, optional token-level logprobs with graceful null fallback, improved streaming stability for function/tool calls, and consistent response formatting to avoid double-escaped JSON in function payloads.
